videos.script: Vereda's payment gateway tells the portal when a patient has paid. The portal has to know two things about that message. Has it been changed on the way? And did it really come from the gateway? {{title}} A checksum answers neither. Anybody who changes the amount just computes a new one. {{checksum}} An HMAC is a checksum with a secret key in it. Only somebody holding the key can produce the right value. {{hmac}} That is how the gateway's messages are protected, and the portal checks each one before it believes it. {{webhooks}} Even a valid message can be sent twice. So a timestamp goes inside what is signed. {{replay}} And when the two sides should not share a secret, a signature does the same job with a key pair. {{signature}}
